slides.kicker: Yash Patil · Applied Compute · The Generalist · 68 min

slides.headline: Frontier models are a **blowtorch.** Most jobs need a knife.
slides.dek: 23-year-old ex-OpenAI post-training researcher. $1.3B company in year one. Trains custom models on private evals for DoorDash, Cognition, and Mercor.
slides.byline: Own or Be Owned · June 2026 · generalist.com/p/own-or-be-owned

slides.text: A model-less company is sitting on **shifting sand.**
slides.author: Yash Patil
slides.role: On Fable 5 guardrails and frontier provider control

slides.heading: Why Fable 5 sparked the own-or-be-owned thesis.
paragraphs: Anthropic's system card flagged restrictions on AI model development queries. Reasonable safety on one reading. Also: the model provider decides what capabilities you get.
If Anthropic holds out a capability for competitive reasons, downstream products built on their API get Sherlocked. The fix is owning your intelligence stack.

slides.sub: Every company codifies what good looks like. Proprietary evals stay home. Goldman and Mercor will never ship scorecards to frontier APIs.

columns.b: Start from open-weight models. RLVR hill climb on customer data. Task-specific, not general.
Deploy in production at scale. Revenue mostly on inference, not training fees.
Capture usage → new training data → continuous loop. Model learns the more you use it.

slides.heading: Customer engagement loop
slides.sub: Applied researchers embed with customer ML teams. Palantir-style FDE model. Platform is the repeatable layer.

slides.heading: DoorDash beat frontier on one narrow task.
slides.body: 100k+ new merchants per year. Unstructured menu photo in. High-fidelity DoorDash storefront out. Build eval → training data → RL → deploy. Specialized model exceeded frontier quality on this workflow.
slides.accentSub: merchants/year · menu photo → storefront · owned intelligence

slides.heading: Post-training stack (how RLVR works)

layers.title: Pre-training
layers.sub: internet-scale data, next-token prediction, sets the floor

layers.title: SFT
layers.sub: behavior cloning on good completion examples

layers.title: RLVR
layers.sub: verifiable rewards, many attempts, hill climb the eval

layers.title: Continuous
layers.sub: sparse rewards from production usage, Cursor Composer-style online RL

slides.sub: Microsoft called it the hill-climbing machine. If you define the hill well, the algorithm works.

slides.heading: Right model for the right task

columns.b: Hardest tasks. Sets the floor. Shared capability. Blowtorch scale.
Your evals. Cost + latency fit. Private data. Raises the ceiling.
Token apocalypse. Inference dominates spend. Better, cheaper, faster open-weight models.

slides.heading: Moat beyond the weights.
paragraphs: Kirkland & Ellis talked about half a billion on AI tools competitors cannot use. The model is part of the moat. Training inside your harness with your context is the rest.
Same model + same frontier API as your competitor = no differentiation. Own the post-training loop on private evals.

columns.b: Sample next problems while training runs. Off-policy corrections. Cut total GPU time on long-horizon tasks.
Sandboxes with codebases and services. Same problem attempted 1,000x. Verifier assigns reward.
Own GPUs. ML infra researchers close to hardware. Environment perf so GPUs never idle on CPU work.

slides.label: Applied Compute valuation, ~14 months in
slides.sub: Ex-OpenAI post-training team. ~2/3 of hires are ex-founders. High-agency FDE culture.

slides.heading: Yash's path to Applied Compute
paragraphs: Stanford dropout (sophomore). Almost landed on ChatGPT engineering. Pulled last-minute to post-training infra. Mentored by Luke Metz, Barret Zoph, John Schulman.
Cold-emailed Sam Altman after a campus dinner. Residency required burning the boats. Lived through the Sam ouster weekend. Hug on the stairs when he returned.

columns.b: AI diffusion is slow. Large institutions resist change. DeployCo exists because deployment is hard.
Even best companies. Messy traces. Field notes from Michael Chan on FDE reality.
Inference demand will balloon. Personal AI × enterprise models. Pareto-optimal cost-performance wins.

slides.text: There is truly some **atrophy** happening by relying too much on AI tools.
slides.author: Yash Patil
slides.role: Recommends The Design of Everyday Things · humans stay overlords

slides.text: Train on your evals. **Keep your moat.**
